newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh police step up hunt for activists.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh police step up hunt for activists.

text.p: Police on Friday stepped up a hunt for anti-government activists as the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) prepared for Sunday's general strike.
"Our actions are also to protest the arrest of four BNP leaders on Thursday and the continuing police search for others," said one BNP youth leader.
Witnesses said thousands of BNP activists participated in a street march and urged Dhaka residents to join the strike.
Many wore T-shirts with pictures of party chief Begum Khaleda Zia and her late husband, former president Ziaur Rahman.
"Let us make the strike a grand success and a turning point in our campaign to topple the government (of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina)," one protester said.

Khaleda made the call for a strike at a party rally in the capital on Wednesday saying: "We can't give them (the government) any more time. They have proved more than inefficient in running the country."

Police said on Friday four BNP leaders arrested in a pre-dawn swoop in the capital on Thursday been detained for one month under the country's Special Powers Act (SPA), and formal charges would be laid soon.
The SPA allows for detention without trial or charges for up to four months.
Those arrested were former BNP ministers Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, Abdul Mannan and Goyeswar Roy, and former Mayor of Dhaka Mirza Abbas.
Police also raided the house of former minister Sadek Hossain Khoka and another BNP leader Salahuddin Ahmed, but both escaped.
Khaleda said the government was on edge since she had called for the strike and was taking extreme measures to suppress its oppenents.
"The arrests only demonstrated the Awami league government's fascist character but we will resist," Khaleda told party workers on Thursday night.

Police told reporters the arrests had nothing to do with Sunday's strike. They said those arrested had been involved with an "extremist BNP group" trying to sabotage the government's development plans and destabilise law and order.
On Friday police also searched for leaders of the radical Jatiya Ganatantrik Party (JAGPA) and the Freedom Party, both of which are staunch allies of the BNP.

JAGPA, a fringe party, is known for its anti-India stance. The Freedom Party was founded by former army officers now on trial for killing Hasina's father and independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in a 1975 coup.

Also on Friday, hundreds of orthodox Moslems demonstrated against Hasina's eight-month-old government in Dhaka. They demanded the prime minister abandon plans to offer India a land transit to send goods and troops to insurgency-ridden northeastern states, and to buy electricity from India.
Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad told a news conference on Thursday none of the deals had been finalised and still required parliament's approval.
